archimate:Folder.name: 4 Value Streams
archimate:Folder.documentation:
The Value Streams component of the SAF articulates how value is created, delivered, and sustained across the statistical enterprise. A value stream represents an end-to-end perspective on how an organization transforms inputs (such as raw data or user requests) into valuable outputs (such as statistical information, research services, or policy insights).
In the SAF, value streams are derived from the organization’s strategic objectives and are closely aligned with GSBPM phases — from Specify Needs through Disseminate and Evaluate. However, while GSBPM provides a functional breakdown of the production process, the value stream perspective emphasizes customer and stakeholder value, highlighting why activities occur and what value they deliver.
Each value stream is composed of interconnected value stages, each of which may involve one or more business processes, functions, and services. This layered design allows the SAF to connect strategic goals to operational execution through a clear line of sight. For instance, the value stream “Provide Access to Data for Research and Innovation” links strategic priorities around data sharing and transparency to underlying capabilities in Data Access Management, Security Governance, and Service Provisioning.
The value stream concept also supports the identification of cross-cutting enablers and dependencies between domains. In a modernized, data-centric statistical organization, value creation often spans multiple systems, departments, and even institutions — for example, when producing integrated datasets or participating in a data space ecosystem. The SAF value streams capture this complexity by modeling the flow of value across organizational and technological boundaries, ensuring interoperability and coherence across national and international levels.
By combining value streams with capability and process mapping, the SAF enables impact-oriented transformation planning. Organizations can identify which parts of the value chain contribute most to strategic outcomes, where bottlenecks exist, and which capabilities should be strengthened to maximize societal and organizational impact.
In essence, the Value Stream layer of the SAF connects the why of strategic motivation to the how of business execution, providing a holistic understanding of value creation across the statistical ecosystem. It positions the organization to evolve from a process-oriented to a value-oriented mindset — focusing not only on efficient production of statistics, but also on the delivery of trusted, relevant, and accessible data that drives insight, innovation, and public good.
